messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into French, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE French line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|--------------------|------------------------|--------| | A | dative preposition “to” (marks the object *you*) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (French omits the preposition) | | te | 2nd‑person singular pronoun, object | te | “you” (object) | OK | | convien | impersonal verb of necessity/obligation | convient | “it behoves / it is proper” | OK | | tenere | infinitive “to hold, to undertake” | prendre | “to take / to undertake” | OK | | altro | adjective “another” | autre | “another” | OK | | vïaggio | noun “journey, course” | chemin | “path, road, course” | OK | | rispuose | 3rd sg. past “he replied” | répondit | “he replied” | OK | | poi | adverb “when, after that” (temporal connective) | quand | “when” | OK | | che | subordinating conjunction “when” (used with *poi*) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (French uses *quand* alone) | | lagrimar | infinitive “to weep” | pleurer | “to weep” | OK | | mi | 1st‑person singular pronoun “me” | me | “me” | OK | | vide | 3rd sg. past “saw” | vit | “saw” | OK | | se | conditional conjunction “if” | Si | “if” | OK | | vuo' | 2nd sg. present of *volere* “wish, want” | veux | “you want / you wish” | OK | | campar | infinitive “to escape” | échapper | “to escape” | OK | | d' | preposition “from, of” (contracted *di*) | à | “to / from” (used with *échapper à*) | OK | | esto | demonstrative adjective “this” | ce | “this” | OK | | loco | noun “place” | lieu | “place, location” | OK | | selvaggio | adjective “savage, wild” | sauvage | “savage, wild” | OK |
---
### Items to Note - **UNNECESSARY**: * A* (preposition “to”) and *che* (conjunction “when”) are not required in French; the meaning is conveyed by the pronoun *te* and the adverb *quand* respectively. - No source words are **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or have **GRAMMAR** issues in the French rendering.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only French script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final French text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line 1** - Original: «Il te convient de prendre un autre chemin», - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- **Line 2** - Original: Il répondit quand il me vit pleurer, - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- **Line 3** - Original: «Si tu veux échapper à ce lieu sauvage»; - Issue: punctuation – the semicolon should be placed inside the quotation marks, as in the source. - Corrected: «Si tu veux échapper à ce lieu sauvage;»
```text «Il te convient de prendre un autre chemin», Il répondit quand il me vit pleurer, «Si tu veux échapper à ce lieu sauvage;» ```
